subject: Transportation Systems
title: Double-Hull Tankers
description: Learn Double-Hull Tankers in one minute.

hook.text: In 1989, the Exxon Valdez spilled 11 million gallons of oil into Alaska's Prince William Sound.

buildup.text: Single-hull tankers had only one layer of steel between crude oil and the ocean.

discovery.text: After the spill, regulations mandated double hulls—two layers of steel with a gap between them.

twist.text: A double hull doesn't prevent all spills, but it survives groundings and collisions that would breach a single hull.

climax.text: By 2015, almost all single-hull tankers were phased out worldwide. Spill rates dropped sharply.

punchline.text: Two layers of steel now stand between oil and ocean.

quiz.question: What event triggered the double-hull tanker regulation?
